Clinical quality within acute surgical care is a critical focus area for healthcare monitoring in [[danmark|Danmark]], primarily tracked through the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]]. The database utilizes specific clinical indicators to evaluate postoperative care standards and patient outcomes, ensuring that high-risk populations receive appropriate monitoring and that mortality rates are rigorously assessed.

One key metric, [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]], evaluates the postoperative monitoring of vulnerable patients. Specifically, it measures the proportion of patients with a high mortality risk—defined as having an ASA score ≥ 3 or being aged ≥ 75 years—who are monitored for at least 24 hours postoperatively in an intermediate care unit or a similar department. According to recent data, this proportion stands at 22.9% (95% CI: 21.1–24.8) across the country [^src1]. 

Additionally, the database tracks survival outcomes through [[indikator-4y|Indikator 4y]], which focuses on mortality following acute surgery. To provide a comprehensive evaluation of clinical quality and long-term patient survival, supplementary calculations are performed for both 30-day and 90-day mortality rates associated with this indicator [^src2]. Together, these metrics form a foundational framework for assessing and improving the quality of acute surgical care.

- Andelen af patienter med høj mortalitetsrisiko (ASA ≥ 3 eller alder ≥ 75 år), der monitoreres ≥ 24 timer postoperativt på et intermediært eller lignende afsnit, er 22,9 % (95 % CI: 21,1–24,8) [^src1] (indikator-5, danmark)
